correctness.rationale: All 242 faces and 715 Hasse incidences are constructed; 110 matched pairs leave one zero-cell and 21 two-cells; a complete topological sort proves matching acyclicity and hence the integral wedge. A separate mod-two boundary computation confirms ranks 10,45,44,11. Exactly 660 full block-preserving permutations are exhaustively generated and checked, signed Lefschetz traces are computed on every group element, and integer character arithmetic yields multiplicity-free constituents of dimensions 10 and 11 with no trivial constituent. The affine group yields one invariant class and the full group none; rational transfer after subdivision proves quotient statements. No finite experiment is used as an infinite theorem.

value.rationale: The 11-point Paley biplane is a canonical symmetric design and a natural directed-neighborhood/Dowker example. The new wedge classification and complete action of the unexpectedly larger 660-element simplicial symmetry group yield a genuine topological distinction: affine quotient rational second homology has rank one, whereas the full quotient is rationally acyclic. Neither existing incidence and group data nor ordinary Betti numbers imply this representation or quotient behavior.
